correctness.summary: The multinomial mode is the Jefferson allocation, so Janson's fixed-proportion seat-excess limit applies in the generic regime. Boundedness gives moment convergence. The Bernoulli-polynomial generating function then cancels to e^w((e^w-1)/w)^(n-2), coefficient extraction gives the stated Stirling formula, and the weighted sum collapses by sum p_i=1. Direct numerical mode enumeration confirms the first four coefficients.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Elezovic 2026 explicitly leaves actual-mode/on-slice coefficient averages open, while Janson 2014 already supplies the necessary Jefferson seat-excess distribution but is not cited there. Searches did not locate the resulting all-orders universal modal Cesaro formula. The claim is limited to the synthesis and closed Bernoulli/Stirling extraction; the underlying apportionment limit theorem and local expansion are prior art. Older rounding-polytope and seat-variance papers remain residual risks.

value.summary: The result closes a stated recent gap, gives every logarithmic modal coefficient average in one explicit dimension-only formula, and reveals an exact cancellation mechanism linking multinomial local asymptotics to classical apportionment probability.

limitations: Only rationally independent generic probability vectors are covered.
Rational/resonant vectors and tie-breaking are not classified.
The universality result is for logarithmic coefficients c_k, not all multiplicative Bell-polynomial coefficients.
No uniformity in k or near resonance is asserted.
Two older apportionment papers identified in REVIEW.md were inspected only through abstracts and bibliographic records.
Independent audit has not been performed.
